newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain, U.S. to discuss 'Open Skies' agreement.
newsitem.headline: Spain, U.S. to discuss 'Open Skies' agreement.

text.p: The United States and Spain will begin talks on Monday on an "Open Skies" agreement to expand civil aviation cooperation, U.S. Secretary of Transportation Federico Pena said on Sunday.
Pena said several joint ventures between American and Spanish airlines were possible and one may involve Spain's Iberia and American Airlines.
"We have been successful in liberalising aviation agreements with many countries throughout the world. One of the ways we have done that is through...an 'Open Skies' agreement," Pena said.
"We are going to have some preliminary discussions tomorrow with the Spanish government about her interest about in possibly having that kind of relationship," he said.
Pena was speaking at a news conference in Toledo where he was attending a forum on promoting business ties between the U.S. and Spain.
"It is possible that there (will be) joint ventures between Spanish and American airlines," he said.
An "Open Skies" agreement would permit Spanish airlines to fly anywhere in the United States and give U.S. airlines similar access to Spain.
"I anticipate it will take some time to finalise (the) discussion but at a minimum, we would like to liberalise the current aviation relationship we have with Spain," Pena said.
In September, Spain's Industry Minister Josep Pique said he expected state-owned Iberia to form an alliance with a foreign company by the end of the year.
He said Iberia was in "intense negotiations" with foreign companies, such as American Airlines, KLM, British Airways.
Pena confirmed on Sunday that Iberia and American Airlines were still negotiating a possible joint venture.
Iberia Chairman Xabier de Irala told a Spanish financial daily earlier this week that Iberia was also in advanced negotiations with Dutch carrier KLM.
